name: freediameter
why: A full Diameter AAA protocol implementation, a rarely examined door into telecom authentication that most developers never see.

brief.what_it_is: freeDiameter is an open source C implementation of the Diameter protocol, which carries Authentication, Authorization and Accounting (AAA) payloads. The README splits it into parts: libfdproto, a shared library for parsing and manipulating Diameter messages and dictionaries; libfdcore, a shared library holding the framework core (peer connections, watchdogs, basic routing, extension loading); freeDiameterd, a small daemon that parses the command line and starts the framework; and extensions that add server applications, advanced routing, or peer management. The README does not spell out a full input/output contract, but in use it takes Diameter peer traffic and a configuration file, and it acts as a server or agent node.
brief.why_it_exists: The README frames Diameter as the successor to RADIUS for AAA traffic and says it is an extensible protocol, with a base protocol (RFC 3588) that every node must support plus application documents such as NAS (RFC 4005) and EAP (RFC 4072). freeDiameter provides a working implementation of that stack.
brief.how_it_works: Applications link libfdcore or run freeDiameterd, which initializes the framework, opens network connections to other Diameter peers, and runs the Base Protocol duties such as watchdogs and routing. Features beyond that base come from extensions that libfdcore loads at startup. The README says that clients which must become Diameter-aware should link libfdcore directly rather than run the daemon.
brief.install_notes: The README only points to an INSTALL file for build and usage details, which I did not fetch. The Homebrew caveats say to edit $HOMEBREW_PREFIX/etc/freeDiameter.conf to taste, that sample configs live in $HOMEBREW_CELLAR/freediameter/1.6.0/share/doc/freediameter, and that contrib files live in $HOMEBREW_PREFIX/opt/freediameter/share/freediameter/contrib. Those caveats are from the brew formula, not the README, and I did not fetch the sample configs.
brief.standout: Diameter is a rarely examined telecom AAA protocol that most developers never meet, and freeDiameter is a full, modular implementation of it rather than a client stub. Its split into a reusable message library, a core framework, and loadable extensions means it can serve as a library for building Diameter-aware software, not just a daemon.
brief.status: Mixed. The project site (freediameter.net) now displays a notice saying the website is no longer maintained and points to an archived copy for documentation. The same notice says the source code is still maintained on GitHub. I did not see a release date or last commit date on the GitHub page, so recent activity is unknown.
brief.caveats: The project website is unmaintained, and the configuration wiki link from the brew caveats returned HTTP 404, so the configuration documentation may be outdated or only available in the archived site. The README notes that RFC 3588 is under revision. The README says the project is not related to an unrelated 'freediameter' project from Sun on SourceForge. I did not read the LICENSE or INSTALL files, so licensing and build requirements are unverified. The README names no platform constraints.
quotes: Diameter is a protocol designed to carry Authentication, Authorization and Accounting (AAA) payload.
It is an evolution of the RADIUS protocol (as the name suggests).
freeDiameter was previously known as the "waaad" project (WIDE AAA Daemon).
